newsitem.title: USA: Two accused of selling girl into marriage in Maine.
newsitem.headline: Two accused of selling girl into marriage in Maine.

text.p: Two people have been charged in connection with an incident in which a 15-year-old girl was allegedly sold into marriage for $250 and some used furniture, police said.

Police on Friday alleged that Abdul Azimi paid Mona Penney for her written permission for her daughter to be married. Maine law requires written parental permission for marriages involving anyone under 18 years old.
Azimi, 29, and the teenager were allegedly married on Nov. 1.

Azimi was indicted late on Friday by a Cumberland County grand jury on charges of sexual assault on a minor, furnishing liquor to a minor and aggravated forgery, according to Portland Police Chief Michael Chitwood.
Azimi has been in jail since early December on charges of assaulting the girl -- allegedly by beating her with a coaxial cable.

Penney was indicted on two counts of endangering the welfare of a child. Penney failed to have her daughter's marriage application reviewed by a probate judge, which is also required for minors, police said.
Azimi denied he offered to buy the mother's permission and that the money and furniture were intended as gifts because Mona Penney needed them, his lawyer Thomas Connolly said.

The Portland Press Herald quoted the girl as saying she met Azimi last May while walking to school. The teen said she thought he was younger and that she was unconcerned about the age difference because she had dated older men.
Penney told the newpaper she initially rejected Azimi's offer and now regrets she accepted it. "I wasn't thinking at the time," she told the paper.
